St. Lucia's Day Filter Coffee

Served at: St. Lucia's Day

Serves 4-6Prep 5 minCook 5-10 min

On St. Lucia's Day, December 13th, families traditionally wake early to celebrate with a special breakfast. Central to this festive morning is a warm cup of coffee, often served alongside saffron buns (lussekatter) and gingerbread cookies. This recipe guides you to brew a robust and comforting coffee, perfect for sharing during this beautiful Swedish tradition.

Ingredients

  • 8 tablespoons (40g) medium-ground coffee beans (preferably freshly ground)
  • 4 cups (960 mL) filtered water
  • Optional: Sugar, milk, or cream to taste

Method

  1. Measure the coffee grounds. For a standard brew, use 2 tablespoons (10g) of coffee for every 6 fluid ounces (180 mL) of water. For 4 cups (960 mL) of water, this means approximately 8 tablespoons (40g) of coffee.
  2. If using whole beans, grind them to a medium consistency, similar to coarse sand, just before brewing.
  3. Pour the measured filtered water into the reservoir of your drip coffee maker.
  4. Place the coffee grounds into a clean filter in the coffee maker's basket.
  5. Turn on the coffee maker and allow it to brew completely.
  6. Once brewing is finished, carefully pour the hot coffee into mugs.
  7. Serve immediately, offering sugar, milk, or cream on the side for guests to customize their cup.

Tips

  • For the best flavor, use freshly roasted whole beans and grind them just before brewing.
  • Adjust the amount of coffee grounds to your preferred strength; add more for a bolder cup or less for a milder one.
  • Enjoy your St. Lucia's Day coffee with traditional Swedish saffron buns (lussekatter) and gingerbread cookies (pepparkakor) for a truly authentic experience.
